text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered for tenant xb-health (dedicated pool xb-dedicated-4). 99th latency > 2s over past 5m and queue length spiking. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tenant_surge

maria: I'm on it, looking at p95/p99 across replicas now. any recent deploys?

alex: no deploys to that pool in last 24h. spike started ~5m ago. p95 -> 1.2s, p99 -> 2.7s, queue depth jumped from 120 -> 980 in 4m. throughput steady.

kevin: sounds like bespoke batching for xb-health is allowing huge batches. check scheduler knob `max_batch_tokens` and per-tenant shaper.

maria: grabbing current config from control-plane...

infra-bot: fetching scheduler config for tenant=xb-health...

infra-bot: config: `max_batch_size: 256, max_batch_tokens: 4096, queue_shaper: disabled, preferred_model: rwx-13b`

jen: that max_batch_tokens is huge for short chat queries. at this load it's creating very long tail queues. we should throttle tenant-level batching and enable queue_shaper.

kevin: agree. propose immediate emergency change: set `max_batch_tokens` -> 1024, enable `queue_shaper: token_based_aggressive`, and add `per_tenant_qos: true`. This should reduce per-request wait and keep throughput. fallback: set tenant to smaller quantized model for burst traffic (rwx-7b-q4) if latency still high.

maria: ok I'm going to apply a hotfix via infra CLI, will target single tenant only.

maria: run: ```bash
redwoodctl scheduler update --tenant xb-health \
  --set max_batch_tokens=1024 \
  --set queue_shaper=token_based_aggressive \
  --set per_tenant_qos=true
```

infra-bot: started job j-8842 to update scheduler (target=xb-health). ETA ~20s. logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/j-8842

alex: watching metrics, gating on p99 and queue length.

(30s later)

infra-bot: job j-8842 succeeded. change rolled to pool xb-dedicated-4 replicas a/c.

jen: tailing inference logs for xb-health: ```
[1845678910] rq=12345 tenant=xb-health batch_tokens=3200 wait_ms=2100
[1845678924] rq=12348 tenant=xb-health batch_tokens=2800 wait_ms=1950
[1845678945] rq=12394 tenant=xb-health batch_tokens=900 wait_ms=420
```

alex: p99 down to 0.9s, queue depth trending down: 980 -> 220 in 3m. nice. :thumbsup:

maria: marking incident mitigation success for now. simone, fyi for customer comms?

simone: saw the pager, thanks for fast action. I'll notify xb-health support lead with note: transient latency spike, mitigation applied (batching knobs reduced), we recommend they stagger large batch jobs or prefer smaller model for heavy burst. will loop in CSM.

kevin: one more proactive tweak: add an emergency routing rule to route any new large requests (>1500 tokens) from xb-health to rwx-7b-q4 for next 10m. rough command: ```json
{
  "tenant":"xb-health",
  "condition":{"tokens_gt":1500},
  "route_to":"rwx-7b-q4",
  "ttl":"10m"
}
```

maria: applying route now. infra-bot kicked off job j-8845, done.

infra-bot: job j-8845 succeeded. 54 requests matched and were routed during the window.

jen: monitoring memory/gpu stats: no OOMs, no additional failures. I recommend leaving queue_shaper for 30m and then gradual rollback to previous config if stable.

kevin: we should also add a per-tenant circuit breaker for sustained queue depth > 500 for > 2m. action item.

maria: noted. creating follow-up ticket ENG-ops: implement per-tenant circuit breaker and safe default max_batch_tokens for dedicated pools.

simone: I'll prep a short customer-facing blurb. no SLA impact expected, they saw elevated latency for ~5-7 minutes.

alex: handing off to daytime oncall (kevin) for follow-up and rollback decisioning. kevin you're up for next 2hrs?

kevin: on it. will keep monitoring and escalate to runtime team if we see tail reappearance.

maria: closing pager, will add timeline to postmortem if needed. thanks all. :pray:
